School Life & Education.title: Different Types of Schools
School Life & Education.text:
Schools around the world are different. Some useful words:

state (public) school: free, run by the government
private school: students' families pay fees
boarding school: students live and sleep at school
vocational school: students learn a job, like cooking or electronics
single-sex / mixed school: only boys or only girls / boys and girls together
homeschooling: children learn at home

Language focus, present simple for facts and routines:
Students at a boarding school live on campus.
The school day starts at 8.30.
We don't wear uniforms. Does your school have a library?

Remember: he / she / it takes -s: She studies at a vocational school.
choices: She goes to a boarding school in England.
She going to a boarding school in England.
She is go to a boarding school in England.
She goed to a boarding school in England.
She go to a boarding school in England.
School Life & Education.explain: Present simple with she: verb + -es. She goes to a boarding school.

School Life & Education.title: Regular and Extracurricular Activities
School Life & Education.text:
Regular activities are lessons in the timetable: maths, history, PE. Extracurricular activities happen outside normal lessons: clubs, school teams, the school choir, the drama club, robotics, volunteering.

Language focus, frequency adverbs:
always (100%) - usually - often - sometimes - rarely - never (0%)
They come before the main verb but after be:
I usually go to the chess club on Tuesdays.
She is always at the library after school.

Asking about frequency:
How often do you play in the school team? Twice a week.

Useful phrases: join a club, take part in a competition, be a member of the team.
School Life & Education.q: Put the adverb in the correct place: I / go / to the robotics club / on Fridays (usually).
choices: I go to usually the robotics club on Fridays.
I go usually to the robotics club on Fridays.
Usually I go to the robotics club on Fridays usually.
I usually go to the robotics club on Fridays.
I go to the robotics club usually on Fridays usually.
School Life & Education.explain: Frequency adverbs come before the main verb: I usually go.

School Life & Education.title: School Anxiety and Stress
School Life & Education.text:
Many students feel stressed before exams or on the first day at a new school. Useful words: anxious, nervous, worried, stressed out, relaxed, confident, pressure, deadline.

Language focus, giving advice with should / shouldn't:
You should get enough sleep before the exam.
You shouldn't study all night.
You should talk to your teacher or the school counsellor.

Other ways to give advice:
Why don't you make a study plan?
It's a good idea to take short breaks.

After should we use the base form of the verb: You should study (not: should to study, should studies).
School Life & Education.q: My friend is very nervous about tomorrow's exam. Which is the best advice?
choices: You should get some rest and review your notes.
You should to stay up all night.
School Life & Education.explain: should + base verb, and the advice is sensible: You should get some rest and review your notes.

School Life & Education.title: National Days and Celebrations
School Life & Education.text:
Every country has national days. In Türkiye we celebrate:
23 April, National Sovereignty and Children's Day
19 May, Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day
30 August, Victory Day
29 October, Republic Day

Language focus, prepositions of time:
on + days and dates: on 29 October, on Monday, on Republic Day
in + months, years, seasons: in October, in 1923, in summer
at + clock times and some holidays: at 9 o'clock, at the weekend (UK), at New Year

Useful verbs: celebrate, decorate, wave flags, watch a parade, give a speech, perform a folk dance.
School Life & Education.q: Republic Day is celebrated ___ 29 October in Türkiye.
School Life & Education.explain: We use on with dates: on 29 October.

Classroom Life & Learning.title: Learning Activities in the Classroom
Classroom Life & Learning.text:
Classroom activities: group work, pair work, presentations, debates, projects, experiments, role-plays, quizzes, brainstorming.

Language focus, present continuous for actions happening now:
subject + am / is / are + verb-ing
Look! The students are doing an experiment.
I am preparing a presentation at the moment.
They aren't listening. Is she taking notes?

Present simple vs present continuous:
We usually work in pairs (routine).
Today we are working in groups (now / temporary).

Time words for continuous: now, right now, at the moment, today, Look!, Listen!
Classroom Life & Learning.q: Be quiet! The teacher ___ the instructions now.
Classroom Life & Learning.explain: Now shows an action in progress: present continuous. The teacher is explaining.

Classroom Life & Learning.title: Personal Learning Styles
Classroom Life & Learning.text:
People learn in different ways:
Visual learners learn best with pictures, charts, colours and mind maps.
Auditory learners learn best by listening: podcasts, discussions, reading aloud.
Kinaesthetic learners learn best by doing: experiments, moving, building models.

Language focus, talking about preferences:
like / love / enjoy / prefer / hate + verb-ing
I enjoy drawing mind maps.
She prefers listening to podcasts.
prefer A to B: I prefer working alone to working in a group.

would rather + base verb:
I'd rather watch a video than read a long text.
Classroom Life & Learning.q: Ali learns best by building models and doing experiments. What kind of learner is he?
Classroom Life & Learning.explain: Learning by doing and moving is the kinaesthetic learning style.

Classroom Life & Learning.title: Learning with Technology
Classroom Life & Learning.text:
Technology in the classroom: smart board, tablet, online platform, educational app, video conference, e-book, artificial intelligence (AI) tools.

Language focus, comparatives:
short adjectives: + -er than: fast → faster than, easy → easier than
long adjectives: more + adjective + than: more useful than, more interesting than
irregular: good → better, bad → worse

E-books are lighter than printed books.
Online quizzes are more fun than paper tests.
A slow internet connection is worse than no connection!

not as + adjective + as: Paper maps are not as practical as GPS apps.
Classroom Life & Learning.q: For me, learning with videos is ___ than reading long texts.
Classroom Life & Learning.explain: Easy is a short adjective ending in -y: y → i + -er, so easier than.

Personal Life and Well-being.title: Body Parts, Illnesses and Diseases
Personal Life and Well-being.text:
Body parts: head, neck, shoulder, chest, stomach, back, arm, elbow, wrist, leg, knee, ankle.

Talking about illness:
I have a headache / a stomachache / a toothache / a sore throat / a fever / a cold / the flu.
My back hurts. I feel dizzy. I've got a cough.

Language focus, what's the matter?
A: What's the matter? / What's wrong?
B: I have a terrible headache.
A: You should take a painkiller and lie down.

Disease vs illness: Disease is often used for a specific medical condition (heart disease, diabetes). Illness is a more general word for being unwell.
Personal Life and Well-being.q: A: What's the matter? B: I ate too much fast food and now I have a ___.
Personal Life and Well-being.explain: Eating too much causes a pain in your stomach: a stomachache.

Personal Life and Well-being.title: Human Nature and Well-being, Today and in the Future
Personal Life and Well-being.text:
Well-being means being healthy and happy in body and mind. Good habits: a balanced diet, regular exercise, enough sleep, spending time in nature, limiting screen time, spending time with friends.

Language focus, making predictions with will:
will + base verb
In the future, people will live longer.
Robots will help elderly people at home.
People won't (will not) need to go to the doctor for small problems; they will use health apps.

We often use will with I think, I'm sure, probably, maybe:
I think we will have smart clothes that check our health.

be going to for predictions with present evidence:
Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
Personal Life and Well-being.q: Which sentence is a prediction about the future?
choices: I think people will use more health apps in the future.
Personal Life and Well-being.explain: I think ... will + verb is used to make predictions about the future.

Personal Life and Well-being.title: Fashion and Personal Fashion Preferences
Personal Life and Well-being.text:
Clothes and fashion words: casual, formal, sporty, trendy, old-fashioned, comfortable, colourful, second-hand, vintage, brand.
Patterns: striped, checked, spotted, plain.

Language focus, order of adjectives:
opinion → size → age → colour → material + noun
a beautiful long old red woollen scarf
She's wearing a nice new blue cotton shirt.

Talking about preferences:
I'm into vintage clothes.
I can't stand tight jeans.
It suits you! (looks good on you)
It fits you. (is the right size)

Sustainable fashion: buying fewer clothes, choosing second-hand items and recycling helps the environment.
Personal Life and Well-being.q: Choose the correct order: She bought a ___ jacket.

Family Life & Home.title: Family Members and Daily Routines, Today and in the Past
Family Life & Home.text:
Family words: parents, siblings, grandparents, cousin, aunt, uncle, nephew, niece, stepmother, only child, extended family, nuclear family.

Language focus, used to for past habits:
used to + base verb shows something that was true in the past but is not true now.
My grandparents used to live in a village.
People didn't use to have mobile phones.
Did your mother use to walk to school?

Compare with present simple:
My grandmother used to bake bread every day, but now she buys it from the bakery.

Note: In negatives and questions with did, we write use to (without -d).
Family Life & Home.q: When my father was a child, he ___ play football in the street every evening, but now he doesn't have time.
Family Life & Home.explain: For a past habit that is not true now: used to + base verb.

Family Life & Home.title: Hobbies and Interests of Family Members
Family Life & Home.text:
Sports: football, basketball, volleyball, swimming, cycling, chess, hiking.
With sports we use:
play + ball games and games: play football, play chess
go + -ing activities: go swimming, go cycling, go hiking
do + individual activities and martial arts: do yoga, do karate, do gymnastics

Films: action, comedy, horror, science fiction, animation, documentary, drama.

Language focus, talking about interests:
be interested in / be keen on / be fond of + noun or verb-ing
My brother is interested in documentaries.
My aunt is keen on doing yoga.
Family Life & Home.q: My sister ___ judo twice a week.
Family Life & Home.explain: We use do with martial arts and individual activities: do judo, do karate, do yoga.

Family Life & Home.title: Different Types of Houses and Families
Family Life & Home.text:
Types of houses: detached house, semi-detached house, terraced house, flat (apartment), cottage, villa, bungalow, tent, igloo, houseboat, stilt house.

Family types: nuclear family (parents and children), extended family (with grandparents, aunts, uncles), single-parent family, blended family (with step-parents and step-siblings).

Language focus, there is / there are:
There is a big garden behind our house.
There are three bedrooms in the flat.
Is there a balcony? Yes, there is.
There isn't any furniture in the attic.

Language focus, comparing places with superlatives:
It's the oldest house in the street.
This is the most comfortable room in our home.
Family Life & Home.q: ___ two bathrooms and a large kitchen in our new flat.
Family Life & Home.explain: Two bathrooms is plural, so we use there are.

Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.title: Activities to Do in Attractions
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.text:
Places in the city: café, cinema, gym, sports club, museum, park, shopping mall, bowling alley, concert hall.

Language focus, making suggestions and invitations:
Let's go to the cinema tonight.
Why don't we try the new café?
How about going to the gym together? (How about / What about + verb-ing)
Would you like to come to the match?

Accepting: That sounds great! / Sure, why not? / I'd love to.
Refusing politely: Sorry, I can't. I have to study. / Maybe another time.

Useful phrases: book a ticket, work out, grab a coffee, hang out with friends.
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.q: How about ___ to the new sports club this weekend?
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.explain: After How about / What about we use verb-ing: How about going ...?

Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.title: Getting Help from Services
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.text:
Services in a neighbourhood: pharmacy (chemist's), hospital, clinic, police station, fire station, post office, bank, municipality, library.

Language focus, asking for help politely:
Could you help me, please?
Can you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?
I'd like to make an appointment with a doctor.
Could I have something for a headache?

Indirect questions are more polite:
Where is the hospital? → Could you tell me where the hospital is?
(In indirect questions the word order is like a sentence: where the hospital is.)

Emergency numbers in Türkiye: 112 (all emergencies).
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.q: Which question is the most polite and grammatically correct?
choices: Could you tell me where is the pharmacy?
Could you tell me where the pharmacy is?
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.explain: In indirect questions we use statement word order: Could you tell me where the pharmacy is?

Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.title: Pros and Cons of Different Types of Transportation
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.text:
Transport: bus, metro (underground), tram, ferry, taxi, bicycle, electric scooter, car, on foot.

Pros (advantages) and cons (disadvantages):
Metro: fast and no traffic, but crowded at rush hour.
Cycling: cheap, healthy and eco-friendly, but dangerous in heavy traffic.
Car: comfortable and flexible, but expensive and it causes pollution.

Language focus, comparatives and superlatives:
The metro is faster than the bus.
Cycling is the cheapest way to get to school.
A car is more comfortable than a bus, but it is the most expensive option.

Linking ideas: However, ... / On the other hand, ... / Although ...
Although the ferry is slow, it is very relaxing.
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.q: In big cities, the metro is usually ___ way to travel during rush hour.
Life in the Neighbourhood, City & Social.explain: Comparing more than two things: superlative. Fast → the fastest.

Life in the World & Culture.title: Continents, Countries and Nationalities
Life in the World & Culture.text:
The seven continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia (Oceania).

Countries and nationalities:
Türkiye → Turkish, Japan → Japanese, Brazil → Brazilian, Spain → Spanish, Germany → German, France → French, China → Chinese, Egypt → Egyptian, the UK → British.

Nationality adjectives and languages always start with a capital letter in English: She is Italian. He speaks French.

Language focus, asking about origin:
Where are you from? I'm from Mexico. I'm Mexican.
Where is she from? She's from Kenya.
What language do they speak in Brazil? They speak Portuguese.
Life in the World & Culture.q: Maria is from Brazil. She is ___, and she speaks Portuguese.
Life in the World & Culture.explain: The nationality adjective for Brazil is Brazilian, written with a capital letter.

Life in the World & Culture.title: Shopping for Food and Food Preferences
Life in the World & Culture.text:
Containers and quantities: a bottle of water, a carton of milk, a loaf of bread, a kilo of tomatoes, a packet of pasta, a can of tuna, a dozen eggs, a jar of honey.

Language focus, countable and uncountable nouns:
Countable: apple, egg, tomato (a / an, many, a few)
Uncountable: milk, rice, sugar, bread, water (some, much, a little)

How many eggs do we need? / How much sugar do we need?
There are a few apples. / There is a little milk.
some in positive sentences and offers, any in negatives and questions:
We need some cheese. We don't have any rice. Have we got any oranges?

At the market: How much is it? / How much are they? It costs 40 lira a kilo.
Life in the World & Culture.q: How ___ rice do we need for dinner?
Life in the World & Culture.explain: Rice is uncountable, so we use How much.

Life in the World & Culture.title: Food and Food Culture from Around the World
Life in the World & Culture.text:
Famous dishes: sushi (Japan), pizza and pasta (Italy), tacos (Mexico), paella (Spain), curry (India), kimchi (Korea), baklava and kebab (Türkiye).

Flavours and textures: spicy, sweet, sour, salty, bitter, crispy, creamy, juicy.
Cooking verbs: boil, fry, bake, grill, roast, chop, slice, stir, mix.

Language focus, the passive (present simple) to describe how food is made:
am / is / are + past participle
Sushi is made with rice and raw fish.
Baklava is baked in the oven.
The vegetables are chopped and fried.
Tea is grown in Rize.

We use the passive when the action is more important than the person who does it.
Life in the World & Culture.q: Turkish coffee ___ in a small pot called a cezve.
Life in the World & Culture.explain: Present simple passive with a singular subject: is + past participle (made).

Life in Nature & Global Problems.title: Natural Resources
Life in Nature & Global Problems.text:
Natural resources are things in nature that people use: water, air, soil, forests, minerals, oil, natural gas, coal, sunlight, wind.

Renewable resources can be replaced naturally: solar energy, wind, water, forests (if we plant trees).
Non-renewable resources will run out one day: oil, coal, natural gas, minerals.

Useful vocabulary: run out of, consume, supply, extract, scarce (rare), fossil fuel.

Language focus, present simple for general truths:
Plants produce oxygen.
Coal comes from ancient plants.
Wind turbines turn wind into electricity.
Life in Nature & Global Problems.q: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
Life in Nature & Global Problems.explain: Coal is a fossil fuel; it takes millions of years to form, so it will run out.

Life in Nature & Global Problems.title: Global Problems Related to Natural Resources
Life in Nature & Global Problems.text:
Global problems: climate change, global warming, air pollution, water shortage, drought, deforestation, plastic pollution, loss of biodiversity, endangered species.

Language focus, cause and effect:
because / because of / so / as a result / lead to / cause
The weather is getting hotter because of greenhouse gases.
People cut down forests, so many animals lose their homes.
Deforestation leads to soil erosion.
As a result, some species become extinct.

Note: because + clause (subject + verb), because of + noun:
The lake dried up because it didn't rain.
The lake dried up because of the drought.
Life in Nature & Global Problems.q: Many fish are dying ___ plastic pollution in the oceans.
Life in Nature & Global Problems.explain: Plastic pollution is a noun phrase, so we use because of.

Life in Nature & Global Problems.title: Protecting Natural Resources
Life in Nature & Global Problems.text:
Ways to protect nature: reduce, reuse, recycle; save water and energy; use public transport; plant trees; avoid single-use plastic; use renewable energy.

Language focus, first conditional for real possibilities:
If + present simple, will + base verb
If we recycle paper, we will save trees.
If people use public transport, there will be less air pollution.
We won't have enough clean water if we don't save it.

Giving strong advice and obligation:
We must protect the forests.
We have to reduce plastic waste.
You mustn't throw rubbish into the sea.
Life in Nature & Global Problems.q: If we ___ off the lights when we leave a room, we will save energy.
Life in Nature & Global Problems.explain: First conditional: If + present simple (turn), will + base verb.

Life in the Universe & the Future.title: Planets and Space
Life in the Universe & the Future.text:
Our solar system has eight planets. In order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

Facts:
Jupiter is the biggest planet.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
Venus is the hottest planet because of its thick atmosphere.
Mars is called the Red Planet.

Space vocabulary: star, galaxy, orbit, moon, comet, asteroid, astronaut, telescope, satellite, gravity, atmosphere.

Language focus, superlatives:
the + adjective-est / the most + adjective
the biggest, the hottest, the coldest, the most interesting
Life in the Universe & the Future.q: Jupiter is ___ planet in our solar system.
Life in the Universe & the Future.explain: We compare Jupiter with all the planets: superlative. Big → the biggest (double g).

Life in the Universe & the Future.title: Life in the Universe
Life in the Universe & the Future.text:
Scientists are looking for life on other planets and moons. For life as we know it, a planet needs liquid water, a suitable temperature, an atmosphere and energy.

Places scientists study: Mars (there may have been water in the past), Europa (a moon of Jupiter with an ocean under the ice), Enceladus (a moon of Saturn).

Language focus, possibility with may / might / could:
There may be life on Europa.
Aliens might exist on distant planets.
Mars could be a home for humans one day.

Certainty: must (almost sure it's true) and can't (almost sure it's not true):
There can't be life on the Sun; it's far too hot.
Life in the Universe & the Future.q: Scientists are not sure, but there ___ be water under the ice on Europa.
Life in the Universe & the Future.explain: When we are not sure, we use may / might / could to express possibility.

Life in the Universe & the Future.title: Space Explorations
Life in the Universe & the Future.text:
Milestones in space exploration:
1957: The first satellite, Sputnik 1.
1961: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space.
1969: Neil Armstrong walked on the Moon.
1998: Building of the International Space Station (ISS) started.
2024: Alper Gezeravcı became the first Turkish astronaut and went to the ISS.

Language focus, past simple for finished events:
regular: walk → walked, explore → explored
irregular: go → went, become → became, fly → flew
When did Armstrong walk on the Moon? He walked on the Moon in 1969.

Present perfect for experiences up to now:
Humans have sent robots to Mars.
No one has visited Jupiter yet.
Life in the Universe & the Future.q: Neil Armstrong ___ on the Moon in 1969.
Life in the Universe & the Future.explain: A finished action at a specific past time (in 1969) takes the past simple: walked.
